QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_56

question.text: Which statement best describes lot sizes across equity, currency, and commodity futures in India?

answer.text: Lot sizes are exchange/product-specific and can change over time — e.g., the Oct 2025 Series VIII workbook example uses a Nifty lot of 65, USDINR is quoted at 1000 USD per lot, and commodity contract specifications list the lot size by product (e.g., Gold contract specifies one kilogram)
All futures have uniform lot sizes of 100 units
Equity lots are always smaller than currency lots which are always smaller than commodity lots
Lot sizes are determined by the trader at the time of order placement

explanation.text: The Logic: Lot sizes are fixed by the exchange and product, not by traders, and they are periodically revised. Series VIII p.32/p.51 illustrates this with a Nifty example lot of 65. Series I p.20 quotes USDINR lot size as 1000 USD. Series XVI commodity contract specifications (pp.141, 146, 188) list lot size by product (for example, Gold one kilogram). The Trap: The previously circulated "Nifty = 25" figure is stale relative to the current workbook example, and specific commodity claims such as "Crude Oil = 100 barrels" are not directly supported on the pages checked. Lot sizes should be quoted from the current exchange specification. Note: Source-backed by Series VIII p.32 and p.51, Series I p.20, and Series XVI pp.141, 146, 188.
